purpose: Assigns a likelihood of clinically significant cancer to a prostate lesion on multiparametric MRI, for detection, localisation and risk stratification in patients with suspected cancer in a treatment-naive prostate.
exam: MRI of the prostate (multiparametric or biparametric)
issuer: American College of Radiology (PI-RADS Steering Committee: ACR, ESUR, AdMeTech Foundation)
system: PI-RADS Prostate Imaging - Reporting and Data System, Version 2.1
aliases: prostate imaging reporting and data system

inputs.label: A finding with a PI-RADS category above 1 is reported
inputs.how_stated: true when any focal lesion, nodule or region of the gland is described for scoring (eg a PI-RADS 2 to 5 lesion, or a lesion given T2W, DWI or DCE scores); false when no such finding is reported, eg 'no focal lesion', 'no suspicious lesion', or only typical BPH change in the transition zone, which PI-RADS treats as a normal variant

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the TZ (How to Score in the TZ: every MRI exam is assigned a category; with no finding above category 1 the exam is PI-RADS 1)

inputs.label: Prostate cancer already treated (MRI for suspected recurrence)
inputs.how_stated: true when the history gives prior treatment of prostate cancer (eg prostatectomy, radiotherapy, focal or ablative therapy) and the MRI looks for recurrence; false for a treatment-naive gland, including suspected cancer, a prior negative biopsy, or BPH treatment

locator.section: Introduction: designed for suspected cancer in treatment naive prostate glands; does not address suspected recurrence following therapy

inputs.label: Zone the lesion is scored in
inputs.how_stated: peripheral for a PZ lesion, transition for a TZ lesion; a central zone or anterior fibromuscular stroma lesion takes the zone it appears to arise from (eg 'scored with TZ criteria') If several lesions are described, read the index lesion only (the highest PI-RADS category; among equals the one with extraprostatic extension, else the largest) and take every lesion value from that one lesion.

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the anterior fibromuscular stroma; Caveats for Overall Assessment (dominant sequence by zone)

inputs.label: DWI score
inputs.how_stated: the DWI (ADC and high b-value) score 1 to 5 as dictated, eg 'DWI 4', 'DWI 3/5'; not assessable when DWI is called X, technically inadequate, non-diagnostic or not performed If several lesions are described, read the index lesion only (the highest PI-RADS category; among equals the one with extraprostatic extension, else the largest) and take every lesion value from that one lesion.

locator.section: Section IV B.2: PI-RADS Assessment of DWI

inputs.label: T2W score
inputs.how_stated: the T2-weighted score 1 to 5 as dictated, eg 'T2 4', 'T2W 2/5'; not assessable when T2W is called X, technically inadequate or not performed If several lesions are described, read the index lesion only (the highest PI-RADS category; among equals the one with extraprostatic extension, else the largest) and take every lesion value from that one lesion.

locator.section: Section IV A.2: PI-RADS Assessment for T2W

inputs.label: DCE
inputs.how_stated: positive for focal early (or contemporaneous) enhancement matching the T2W or DWI finding; negative for no early enhancement, diffuse enhancement, or enhancement of a BPH-type nodule; not assessable when DCE is X, inadequate or not given (biparametric MRI) If several lesions are described, read the index lesion only (the highest PI-RADS category; among equals the one with extraprostatic extension, else the largest) and take every lesion value from that one lesion.

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS 1 overall for the examination: no finding above category 1; clinically significant cancer is highly unlikely.
outcomes.recommendation: PI-RADS states biopsy should not be considered for category 1; it gives no management, which rests on clinical factors and local practice.
caveats: Every MRI exam is assigned a category; typical BPH nodules alone are a normal variant (T2W 1) and need not be reported separately.
The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.
If DWI was inadequate or not performed, the report should clearly acknowledge this limitation.

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the TZ (How to Score in the TZ: with no finding above category 1 the exam is PI-RADS 1); the MRI-findings-only caveat from p 17 (Assessment and Reporting); the inadequate-DWI caveat from p 22 (Caveats for Overall Assessment)

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS 1: very low; clinically significant cancer is highly unlikely to be present.
outcomes.recommendation: PI-RADS states biopsy should not be considered for category 1; it gives no management, which rests on clinical factors and local practice.
caveats: The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.
If DWI was inadequate or not performed, the report should clearly acknowledge this limitation.
With several lesions this scores the index lesion only (highest category; among equals the one with EPE, else the largest; S1 p 19).

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS 2: low; clinically significant cancer is unlikely to be present.
outcomes.recommendation: PI-RADS states biopsy should not be considered for category 2; it gives no management, which rests on clinical factors and local practice.
caveats: The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.
If DWI was inadequate or not performed, the report should clearly acknowledge this limitation.
With several lesions this scores the index lesion only (highest category; among equals the one with EPE, else the largest; S1 p 19).

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS 3: intermediate; the presence of clinically significant cancer is equivocal.
outcomes.recommendation: Biopsy may or may not be appropriate, depending on factors other than the MRI; PI-RADS gives no management recommendation.
caveats: The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.
In the PZ, a DWI 3 lesion without adequate DCE (eg biparametric MRI) stays category 3 and is not upgraded.
In the PZ or CZ, an encapsulated, circumscribed, round nodule is likely an extruded BPH nodule and should be category 2, even if hypointense on ADC.
If DWI was inadequate or not performed, the report should clearly acknowledge this limitation.
With several lesions this scores the index lesion only (highest category; among equals the one with EPE, else the largest; S1 p 19).

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS 4: high; clinically significant cancer is likely to be present.
outcomes.recommendation: PI-RADS states biopsy should be considered; it gives no further management, which rests on clinical factors and local practice.
caveats: The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.
In the PZ or CZ, an encapsulated, circumscribed, round nodule is likely an extruded BPH nodule and should be category 2, even if hypointense on ADC.
If DWI was inadequate or not performed, the report should clearly acknowledge this limitation.
With several lesions this scores the index lesion only (highest category; among equals the one with EPE, else the largest; S1 p 19).

caveats: The category rests on the MRI findings only, not PSA, rectal examination, history or planned treatment.

outcomes.classification: No PI-RADS category: DWI and DCE are both inadequate or absent, so assessment is limited to staging (extraprostatic extension).
outcomes.recommendation: Limit the assessment to staging for extraprostatic extension; state the limitation in the report.
caveats: When DWI is inadequate, PI-RADS advises repeating it if the cause of failure can be remedied.

outcomes.classification: Does not fit a PI-RADS v2.1 category: T2W is inadequate (X), and the source gives no assessment table without T2W.
outcomes.recommendation: No category from the PI-RADS tables; state the inadequate T2W sequence in the report.
caveats: Library addition: PI-RADS v2.1 gives assessment tables only for an inadequate DWI or DCE, not for an inadequate T2W.

outcomes.classification: PI-RADS v2.1 does not apply: it is designed for treatment-naive glands, and its assessment criteria do not apply to suspected recurrence after treatment.
outcomes.recommendation: No PI-RADS category; v2.1 criteria do not apply to suspected recurrence after treatment.

summary.text: PI-RADS v2.1 gives each prostate lesion a 5-point category for the likelihood that its T2W, DWI and DCE findings correspond to clinically significant cancer.

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting

summary.text: DWI is the dominant sequence in the PZ and T2W in the TZ. DCE matters only to upgrade a PZ DWI 3 lesion to 4, or when DWI is inadequate.

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting; Caveats for Overall Assessment (p 21)

summary.text: In the TZ, an atypical nodule (T2W 2) is upgraded to 3 by DWI 4 or 5; T2W 1 or 2 is not upgraded by DWI 3.

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the TZ (How to Score in the TZ)

summary.text: PI-RADS gives no management recommendations: biopsy should be considered for 4 or 5, not for 1 or 2, and may or may not suit a 3.

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting

definitions.text: Clinically significant cancer (for PI-RADS): on pathology, Gleason score > 7 as printed (including 3+4 with a prominent but not predominant Gleason 4 component), and/or volume > 0.5 cc, and/or extraprostatic extension.

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting

definitions.text: Positive DCE: enhancement that is focal, earlier than or contemporaneous with adjacent normal prostate, and corresponds to a suspicious T2W and/or DWI finding.

locator.section: Section IV C: Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced (DCE) MRI

definitions.text: Negative DCE: no early or contemporaneous enhancement; diffuse multifocal enhancement not matching a focal T2W or DWI finding; or focal enhancement of a lesion with BPH features on T2W (including extruded BPH in the PZ).

locator.section: Section IV C.2: PI-RADS Assessment for DCE

definitions.text: 'Markedly' (DWI category 4): a more pronounced signal change than any other focus in the same zone.

locator.section: Section IV B.3: Caveats for DWI

definitions.text: Category X: a component (T2W, DWI or DCE) that is technically inadequate or was not performed.

locator.section: Section III: Caveats for Overall Assessment

definitions.text: Index lesion: the lesion with the highest category; among equals, the one with extraprostatic extension, else the largest. Up to four lesions of category 3 to 5 may be reported.

tables.title: T2W score, peripheral zone
rows: Linear or wedge-shaped hypointensity, or diffuse mild hypointensity, usually with an indistinct margin
Heterogeneous signal, or non-circumscribed, rounded, moderate hypointensity; includes others not qualifying as 2, 4 or 5
Circumscribed, homogeneous, moderately hypointense focus or mass confined to the prostate and under 1.5 cm in greatest dimension
As 4 but 1.5 cm or more in greatest dimension, or definite extraprostatic extension or invasive behaviour

tables.title: T2W score, transition zone
rows: Normal-appearing TZ (rare) or a round, completely encapsulated nodule ('typical nodule')
A mostly encapsulated nodule, or a homogeneous circumscribed nodule without encapsulation ('atypical nodule'), or a homogeneous mildly hypointense area between nodules
Heterogeneous signal with obscured margins; includes others not qualifying as 2, 4 or 5
Lenticular or non-circumscribed, homogeneous, moderately hypointense, and under 1.5 cm in greatest dimension
As 4 but 1.5 cm or more in greatest dimension, or definite extraprostatic extension or invasive behaviour

rows: No abnormality on ADC and high b-value DWI
Linear or wedge-shaped hypointensity on ADC and/or linear or wedge-shaped hyperintensity on high b-value DWI
Focal (discrete, different from background) hypointensity on ADC and/or focal hyperintensity on high b-value DWI; may be marked on ADC or on high b-value DWI, but not both
Focal, markedly hypointense on ADC and markedly hyperintense on high b-value DWI; under 1.5 cm in greatest dimension
As 4 but 1.5 cm or more in greatest dimension, or definite extraprostatic extension or invasive behaviour

Focal, and earlier than or contemporaneous with enhancement of adjacent normal prostate, and matching a suspicious T2W and/or DWI finding

pitfalls.text: Not for suspected recurrence after prostate cancer treatment; the source also does not address progression during active surveillance.

locator.section: Introduction

pitfalls.text: Zone decides the dominant sequence. A central zone or anterior fibromuscular stroma lesion is scored with the criteria of the zone it appears to arise from.

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the anterior fibromuscular stroma; Caveats for Overall Assessment

pitfalls.text: An encapsulated, circumscribed, round nodule in the PZ or CZ is likely an extruded BPH nodule and should be category 2, even if hypointense on ADC.

locator.section: Section IV B.3: Caveats for DWI

pitfalls.text: Typical TZ BPH nodules (round, circumscribed, encapsulated) are a normal variant, score T2W 1 and need no separate report, even if they restrict or enhance.

locator.section: Section III: Evaluation of the TZ; Caveats for Overall Assessment (p 22)

pitfalls.text: Assign the category on MRI findings only; PSA, rectal examination, clinical history and planned treatment do not enter it.

locator.section: Section III: Assessment and Reporting

pitfalls.text: Prostatitis can change PZ signal on every sequence; mild T2W or DWI change that is indistinct, linear, lobar or diffuse rather than rounded is less likely malignant.

locator.section: Section III: Caveats for Overall Assessment

pitfalls.text: Inadequate or absent DWI should usually prompt a repeat of DWI if the cause can be remedied; otherwise assess without it and state the limitation clearly.
